chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The people are upon six divisions, which all return to three divisions: Faith, Disbelief, and Straying. And they are the People of the Two Promises, whom Allah has promised Paradise and Hell: The Believers and the Disbelievers; The Weak and the Hopeful for Allah's Command, either He punishes them or He repents for them; And those who confess their sins, who mixed a righteous deed with an evil one; And the People of Al-A'raf.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْوَعْدَيْن: People of the Two Promises (Paradise and Hell)

ai.seo_question: What are the six divisions of people according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates six distinct categories of humanity, which ultimately converge into three eschatological outcomes: Faith, Disbelief, and Straying. This classification highlights the 'People of the Heights' (Ahl al-A'raf) as a unique intermediate group, often interpreted in Shia scholarship as those whose good and bad deeds are balanced, awaiting Allah's final mercy or judgment. The hadith underscores the theological concept of 'Ahl al-Wa'dayn' (People of the Two Promises), linking the Believers and Disbelievers to their respective eternal destinations of Paradise and Hell.
